mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average for two consecutive months, investors anticipate future rate cuts, lowering real discount rates and boosting equity present-value pricing, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < avg(FEDFUNDS) over the past 12 months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 12-month pre-trigger average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, prompting equity market optimism and higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month AND UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 out of the next 40 triggered months, SPX 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the labor signal (p > 0.25 in a binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above trend for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which lowers real interest rates via monetary policy anticipation and supports higher S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO_trend + 1.5 SD for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: During the 5-day horizon following the trigger, SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of similar windows (rolling 30-day window mean).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests the Fed is less likely to raise rates, lowering financing costs and supporting higher S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 AND CPIAUCSL decreases by > 0.3 percentage points in one month
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive 20-day windows with the CPIAUCSL signal, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of residential investment to GDP (not directly observable in the catalog) is inferred from housing starts (HOUST) rising above trend, it predicts upcoming fiscal stimulus and a subsequent decline in real rates, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > HOUST_trend + 1 SD for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 4 out of the next 8 windows matching the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.2 in a sign test).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in job openings (not directly observable; proxy via complement: monthly change in employment (PAYEMS) minus monthly change in unemployment (UNRATE) turns negative) suggests tight labor markets, which can cause equity market stress and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 10 consecutive triggered windows, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.25 in a binomial test).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for four consecutive months, in the absence of other demand signals, is interpreted as structural supply-side easing and predicts positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2.0 for 4 consecutive months AND no concurrent demand proxy crosses a positive threshold
failure_condition: Across 20 such 5-day windows, SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.15 in a paired t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the monthly change in retail sales (not directly observable; proxy via RSAFS) accompanied by a sustained increase in the S&P 500 itself (not directly observable; proxy via SPX level) indicates market expectations of rate cuts, which can produce positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by > 3% month-over-month AND GDPC1 increases by > 2% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In 6 out of the next 12 triggered windows, SPX 20-day forward returns are not positive (p > 0.25 in a sign test).
